findings.claim: Tool 1 compares only '## A<n>:' sections, so frozen-copy bytes outside them are never compared with the read copy. Each of these passes tool 1 with no disposition (TESTED, E1-E7): a later or changed ruling under a near-miss heading ('## A107 :', '## A107.', '##  A107:', '## a107:', '## A107 —'), a '## A62 (correction):' section, or preamble text. It also passes on REAL prereg r6 d28c95f5 with its read copy c01b3c51 (I10, I11, I12: PASS with dispositions_required [] and changed_sections []). Tool 4 builds a SEAL_RECORD when the open V005 holds the same bytes (E8; the open V005 is modelled by a SYNTHETIC r12 copy citing the variant). README L237 and build note B-N2 disclose only the preamble, and only for c01b3c51. For the r6 seal this is not reachable while root enforces A106.3 (frozen copy == c01b3c51, r6 checklist B1): with --expect-frozen-sha c01b3c51 tool 1 refuses FROZEN_SHA_MISMATCH (I10x-I12x), and tool 2 with the real compare ties the frozen sha to the open V005 bytes. But a tool 1 PASS with no dispositions does not show that the frozen copy equals the read copy, and the README's B1 command omits --expect-frozen-sha.
findings.fix: In tool 1, remove every '## A<n>:' section from both copies and refuse if the remaining bytes (the preamble and any non-entry '## ' section) differ, for example with NON_ENTRY_BYTES_CHANGED. Alternatively, refuse any '## ' heading line in either copy that is not an entry heading. For the r6 seal now: pass --expect-frozen-sha c01b3c51e34501d77e474594cc0b4be72c6e068c7f58a595055316313a8d4bb1 at B1, in the README command and in Claude3's script.

findings.claim: The 0640 substring test accepts a changed_text with no content. On the suite's C-01 fixture (a substantive edit inside A62), a no_change_after_change row passes with each of these (TESTED): 'Y' (1 byte, the shortest new excerpt; B1), the single character U+00E9 (B2), and the whitespace-only '\t' for an edit containing a tab (B3). This is the PV-D05-1 class: a nominal disposition of a changed entry. It contradicts three claims: tool 1's header ('so a generic string never passes'), the changed_text_codes docstring, and README L61 ('A generic string never satisfies changed_text'). It also contradicts the premise of 0640. The code follows the literal rule. Not reachable for the r6 seal, where CH is empty (I1, I13, I15).
findings.fix: Require changed_text to be non-blank and to contain the whole changed span of the new section: new[p:len(new)-s], where p and s are the common prefix and suffix of the old and new sections (or every inserted or replaced line of a line diff). For a pure deletion, require revised. Alternatively, ask root to rule a minimum. Then correct the three claims.

findings.claim: The check that prereg_revision is not the prereg compares only the resolved path and the sha of the prereg that tool 1 is given. Through tools 3 and 4, that prereg is the SEALED prereg. So a revised row whose prereg_revision pins the TEXT OF RECORD (the same document before the slots are filled) passes tool 3 (D3), and tool 4 builds a SEAL_RECORD carrying it (D4). In tool 1 directly, two copies of the prereg also pass: the prereg plus one trailing newline (D1), and the prereg re-serialized (D2). Any other pinned file is accepted too: the frozen copy, the read copy, the open V005 (D5-D7; Codex1 0093 and README L65 disclose this class). A symlink to the prereg is refused (D8). Not reachable for the r6 seal, which needs no dispositions file. TESTED.
findings.fix: Tool 3 passes the text-of-record pin to tool 1 as a forbidden revision. Tool 1 also refuses a revision that parses as JSON whose content equals the prereg's once the seal_slots values are blanked. Optionally, require the revision to be a prereg (schema and revision fields) whose text differs.

Result: RECORD_BUILT; the record's prereg is the sealed prereg, and its recorded prereg_revision is the text of record.

findings.claim: 'Non-empty after strip' is implemented with Python's str.strip(), which keeps format and control characters. A reason made only of U+200B, U+FEFF, U+2060, U+0000 or U+00AD passes tool 1 (C1-C5). So does a why_no_prereg_effect made only of U+200B (C7). Tool 4 builds a SEAL_RECORD whose reason is '​' (C8). A reason of NBSP plus U+3000 is refused (C6). Not reachable for the r6 seal. TESTED.
findings.fix: nonblank(x) requires at least one character whose unicodedata category does not start with Z or C. Apply the same test to changed_text.

findings.claim: Two simulated races (TESTED). Tool 1 reads the frozen file three times: for its sha, its text and its sections (inherited from r2). Tool 4 pins a fresh sha of the sealed prereg, taken after tools 3 and 1 checked it. F1: the frozen file is swapped to unedited bytes after its first read; tool 1 then passes an undisposed A62 edit while pinning the edited file's sha 059aecea. F2: the sealed prereg is rewritten after tool 3; tool 4 then builds a record pinning prereg c2ca0485, while tool 3 verified 862c08fe. Downstream, both fail closed (FORMAL): the sealed compare refuses any prereg other than its V007_PREREG_SHA256 (r13 L5674-5676), and with the real compare, tool 2 ties the frozen sha to the open V005 bytes (r13 L1241). The dispositions file is already read once and re-verified (TESTED by the suite).
findings.fix: Read each input once, and hash, decode and section those same bytes. Tool 4 pins tool 3's verified sealed_prereg {path, sha256} and refuses if a re-hash differs, as DISPOSITIONS_CHANGED_AFTER_CHECK already does for the dispositions file.

result.summary:
REFUTE stage. Folder: claude_artifacts/v007_final_prereg_c4/seal_tools_v003_refute (new; no stopped run existed). seal_tools_v003 was only read.

Method (everything TESTED unless labelled):
- All 13 build files and both tool pins re-hashed and equal the build result. The HASHES manifest re-verifies 442/442 by sha and size, after all my runs.
- Copies of the six sources, the suite, r2 and the fence were made into the refute folder.
- Bypass probes ran from a work copy of the suite: the published test plus five lines that call probes/refute_probes_c4v003r.py, which reuses main()'s fixtures. 78 probes; record REFUTER_PROBES_C4R001.json fe0ff1d3.

Holds as specified:
- Bare names: refused via the tool 4 API string form, the tool 3 empty-name form, tool 1 CLI forms (no value, after '--', '=' empty), tool 4 admission mode and the tool 3 CLI (A1-A7).
- changed_text spanning the A62/A63 boundary, in another case, or with NBSP for spaces: refused (B4-B6).
- A prereg_revision symlink to the prereg: refused (D8).
- Strict-JSON defects (invalid UTF-8, encoded surrogate, escaped duplicate key, trailing data, UTF-32, 1e400): refused with typed codes (G2-G7).
- Unicode-whitespace reason: refused (C6).
- REAL r6: tool 1 passes with L u CH empty. C-01 edits at A47, A62, A81 and A106 refuse. Plain no_change on A62 refuses. r5's read copy refuses.
- On r6x (r6 with one leaf, path_to_be, in the run folder), with r13 and the real case block 76309ae3: tool 3 passes; tool 4 builds a SEAL_RECORD with later_entry_dispositions NOT_SUPPLIED_NONE_REQUIRED; the admission check passes; the real guard v008 admits it; both W7-S1 configs refuse.
- The real r6 bytes refuse only on the CLAUDE2 path_to_be.
- B8: v003 is stricter than the guard. A record with duplicate sealed_by keys is refused by v003 and admitted by guard v008 (FORMAL from the guard source, TESTED in J3).
- The CLAUDE2 control path has no symlink component, so D-10 holds once root creates the frozen copy there.
- An independent section splitter confirms: r5 CH = [] and L = A102-A106; the r6 read copy equals the closed V005; c01b3c51 has no non-entry headings.
- V005 stores entries out of numeric order (A47-A77, A106 down to A78, A76, A75, A65). An EOF append therefore changes A65, and tool 1 catches it (E2e, I11e).

Regression (TESTED):
- Every changed source line against r2 is header, rename, D-05 (0633, 0640, C-01) or B8. Tools 2 and 5 change only header and renames.
- The DELTA hunk ranges equal difflib opcodes for all six sources, and its reason counts match (DELTA_CROSSCHECK_C4R001.txt).
- Mutation record: all 78 results files re-hash and fail at least one case. 73 ran 352 cases. Five ran 345 (M54, M55, M58, M59, M66): the genuine build refused and the record-dependent block was skipped. They are still kills.
- README and DELTA claims agree with the code, except the README claims in R-02 and R-07.

UNTESTED: the real seal; root's frozen copy at CLAUDE2; Claude3's script wiring; whether any reason or revision is adequate; mutants were not re-run, only their records re-verified.

Process notes:
- About 00:13Z: one `echo ==========` hit zsh `=` expansion (rule 4). It errored before running and wrote nothing.
- Probe run 1 stopped on my own assertion (the closed V005 has no final newline), so it printed no fence summary. In run 2, I15 hit a fixture key-map mismatch. Both were fixed; run 3 is the record.
- The harness captured two lines of background stdout (timestamps and rc) in the session's tasks/ directory, not in the scratchpad. All real output is in the refute folder.
- At each start-up the fence probes call realpath on non-existent runs_ext and UVT probe paths (FORMAL, as the build disclosed). Nothing else touched runs_ext, C5H, UVT or target data.
- No launch, no compare run, no --validity-only, no deletes, moves or network. Nothing was written outside the refute folder.
result.verdict: REFUTE: 0 BLOCKING, 4 SHOULD_FIX, 3 NOTE. No bypass reaches the r6 seal path. With prereg r6 d28c95f5, its read copy c01b3c51 and a frozen copy equal to c01b3c51, L u CH is empty and these all pass (TESTED): v003 tools 1, 3 and 4, the admission check and the real guard v008. As specified, these all refuse: bare names by every entry point, PV-D05-1 as fixtured, C-01 (including A47, A62, A81 and A106 edits on r6), a wrong read copy, the strict-JSON defects, B8 and W7-S1. Still, 31 of 78 refuter probes pass where the intent of the D-05 rule says they must not. They group into four SHOULD_FIX findings: frozen-copy bytes outside entry sections are never compared (R-01); a one-character or whitespace changed_text passes (R-02); prereg_revision can point to the prereg itself in another byte form (R-03); a reason made only of invisible characters passes (R-04). R-01 and R-02 contradict published claims. The three NOTEs: a simulated TOCTOU (R-05), an untyped refusal for a lone surrogate (R-06), and stale "r6 UNTESTED" claims (R-07).
